ai.description: *Tropidophorus assamensis* reaches 15 cm. It is brown with dark transverse bands and a pale belly. Key features include strongly keeled scales and a semi-aquatic habit. Family: Scincidae.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Tropidophorus assamensis* is uniquely distinguished by its strongly keeled, overlapping scales and the presence of a distinct, deep groove along the center of its belly.
ai.habitat: *Tropidophorus assamensis* inhabits humid, evergreen broadleaf forests in Northeast India, typically found near rocky streams at elevations between 500 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The North-Eastern Waterskink is primarily diurnal and semi-aquatic, often retreating into water or under damp leaf litter when threatened to evade potential predators.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Tropidophorus assamensis* is ovoviviparous, producing small litters of 2–4 live young. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, from June to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Tropidophorus assamensis* is endemic to Northeast India, specifically found in Assam and Arunachal Pradesh at elevations between 200 and 1,000 meters.
